belief: I have to earn my parents' love.
origins: Where affection was given for achievement and withdrawn for failure, children learn that love is a wage. Praise for grades, sports, or good behavior, and coldness for mistakes, teach that we are loved for what we do. As adults we may still perform for parents, or for others, hoping the reward will finally come.
teaches: Paul writes, “God proves His love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” He says, “For it is by grace you have been saved through faith, and this not from yourselves; it is the gift of God, not by works.” John writes, “We love because He first loved us.” God’s love is given before we do anything, and it is not taken back when we fail. A parent’s conditional love is a wound, but it does not set the terms for how God loves you, and you do not have to keep paying a debt you never owed.
self_statements: If I stop achieving, they will stop caring.
Love is something I have to deserve.
I have to keep proving myself.
When I fail, I lose their love.
Their love is always one mistake away.
errors: Predicting loss of love if I stop performing.
Seeing love as either earned or absent.
Insisting that I must keep earning their approval.
Feeling anxious about failing and treating it as proof of risk.
questions: When did I first learn that love had a price?
What happened when I failed or disappointed them?
If their love really is conditional, whose problem is that?
What is the difference between earning love and receiving it?
How did God love me before I did anything?
What would I do differently if I believed I was already loved?
truth: Love that must be earned is not the kind of love God gives. I am loved by God before I do anything. I can care for my parents and respect them without trying to purchase what should be freely given.
hw_truths: God’s love is given, not earned.
Christ died for me while I was still a sinner.
I do not have to pay a debt I never owed.
I love because He first loved me.
I am loved before I do anything.
log: Each morning, say “I am loved before I do anything today,” and note one task done from love, not fear.
actions: Write what you had to do to get approval as a child.
Let it sink in that He loved you at your worst.
Show kindness this week without expecting anything back.
Tell a trusted friend or counselor about the conditions you grew up with.
prayer: Lord, I have worked for love all my life. Thank You that You loved me while I was still a sinner. Teach me to receive Your love as a gift and to stop paying for what You freely give. Amen.
hw_questions: When did I learn love had a price?
What would I do if I knew I was loved?
What can I do with no reward?
name_example: Sarah can write: “Christ loved me while I was still a sinner, so I do not have to earn love.”
